question: What is the Colorado SAR Archive?
answer: An independent collection of reported search and rescue incidents in Colorado. Each record brings together a summary, location, and available source reports. It is a historical reference, not a live rescue service or an official count of all incidents.

question: How complete is the data?
answer: Coverage varies by year, place, and responding agency. A place with more records is not necessarily more dangerous, and a year with fewer records does not necessarily mean fewer rescues. Some dates, outcomes, and other details may be approximate or inferred; read the notes and original sources.

question: How are incidents selected and verified?
answer: Entries collect reported Colorado search and rescue incidents from public sources. Contributors provide source links and document uncertainty; the maintainer reviews submissions and duplicate candidates before promotion. Inclusion is not independent verification of every reported fact. Check the original reports and notes.

question: How can I contribute or correct a record?
answer: Follow the [contribution guide](https://github.com/dgriff03/colorado-sar-archive/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Submit one JSON file per new incident, or propose a correction to the existing record with supporting sources and its stable ID. You can also open an issue; please do not include private medical or contact information.

question: Can I reuse the data?
answer: The MIT license applies to project code, not the incident dataset or linked reporting. Dataset redistribution terms are still under maintainer review. Source publishers retain their rights; availability for download is not an additional license grant.

question: Who maintains this archive?
answer: Daniel ([@dgriff03](https://github.com/dgriff03)) maintains this independent archive. It is not an official SAR agency service. Contributions are reviewed through the public repository.

question: Does this site use analytics?
answer: Google Analytics collection is currently paused while automatic URL tracking is disabled. The replacement configuration allows only coarse page names, without search queries, incident IDs, titles, hashes or referrers. It respects Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control. Search filters remain in shareable URLs, so avoid entering private information.
